issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order is inconsistent between the problem specification/UML and the template. The problem statement and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first), but the template's Meal constructor is declared as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first). This will confuse students and make the example code in Main (and the UML) incompatible with the provided template Meal class.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java in the template to match the specification and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). Also ensure any example usage in Main (commented code) and documentation uses the same parameter order (name first) so students have consistent examples.

issues.description: Constructor parameter ordering for the Meal class is inconsistent: the problem statement UML and the solution implementation use Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template Meal.java declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will confuse students and cause code examples (and the intended usage in Main and the problem description) to fail to compile or map to the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the template Meal.java to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so it matches the problem statement and the solution (or alternatively, update all usage sites to match the template signature). Prefer aligning the template to the problem/solution signature to avoid student confusion.
